text:
saira: quick heads up — new bring-up for orpheus-embed (int6) on the multilingual holdout shows a surprising dip in recall@10. posting raw checks below, can someone take a look?

tom: thanks. can you paste the eval stats? small diffs sometimes from index params or whitening.

saira: sure — baseline float32 vs int6 (same checkpoint, quant pipeline = symmetric per-tensor):
```
Model: orpheus-embed-v1
Dataset: multi-holdout-8k
Float32: recall@1 0.713, recall@5 0.842, recall@10 0.890
Int6:    recall@1 0.707, recall@5 0.824, recall@10 0.830
```

leah: whoa that recall@10 delta (~6 points) is big. recall@1 small so top-1 preserved but tail lost — smells like neighborhood distortion. did you use the same HNSW params and normalization?

saira: yes same HNSW M=16 ef_construction=200, ef_search=128 for both runs. I did L2 normalize before indexing in float32 run, but in int6 run I normalized after dequant (same codepath).

eva: can you dump the norm stats pre/post quant? sometimes quant shifts mean length and that changes cosine similarity ordering.

saira: quick norm check (float vs int6 raw embs):
```
# quick python snippet used
import numpy as np
# embs_float shape (8000, 768)
# embs_int6 same shape
print('float mean,std', np.linalg.norm(embs_float,axis=1).mean(), np.linalg.norm(embs_float,axis=1).std())
print('int6  mean,std', np.linalg.norm(embs_int6,axis=1).mean(), np.linalg.norm(embs_int6,axis=1).std())
```
Outputs:
float mean,std 1.02 0.04
int6  mean,std 0.81 0.12

tom: that explains a lot — norms collapse after int6. if you L2-normalize after quantization the vectors should be comparable for cosine, but if any whitening/centering happens before quant then it will be wrong. did you apply our whitening transform before quantizing?

saira: i did quant of the raw linear outputs (no whitening), then downstream pipeline applies a small centering step in the index pipeline (legacy). float32 path had centering before quant, int6 path had centering after dequant — messed ordering.

leah: ordering bug is a likely root cause. two quick experiments to confirm: 1) force L2-normalize post-dequant and re-eval; 2) try per-channel (pq-like) scaling / per-channel quant vs per-tensor to see if mean shift reduces.

eva: also try cosine vs inner product in the HNSW search — if norms differ a lot, inner product will penalize shorter vectors more. set ef_search=256 for the test to reduce search noise.

ci-bot: pipeline-run(orpheus-int6-norm-fix) finished — status: queued

saira: ran the quick L2-normalize-after-dequant test and a reindex with ef_search=256. results:
```
Int6 + L2-postnorm: recall@1 0.712, recall@5 0.839, recall@10 0.886
Int6 + per-channel-quant (symm): recall@10 0.871
Int6 (orig): recall@10 0.830
```

tom: nice — normalizing after dequant recovers almost all the gap. per-channel helps a bit but not as much as correcting the ops ordering.

leah: so actionable: 1) fix transform ordering in quant pipeline (apply whitening/centering before quant), 2) add a unit test that asserts post-quant norm distribution within X sigma of float baseline, 3) rerun full sweep with ef_search=256 and record recall@k diff.

eva: also add an eval that records pairwise cosine drift histogram and a small UMAP snapshot (we can store a tiny png link). i noticed cluster shapes change in quick UMAP after the bad ordering — here's a temp link: https://artifacts.redwood.dev/umaps/orpheus-int6-quick.png

saira: noted — i'll open a PR to reorder ops + add the norm assertion. assigning ownership: i'll do the pipeline fix, tom you take the HNSW reindexing sweep, leah add the unit/eval checks, eva add the UMAP artifact and histogram.

tom: acked. also suggest adding a brief README in the quant folder about required pre-quant transforms to avoid regressions. small doc goes a long way.

saira: thanks all — will follow up with PR link and updated numbers. closing the triage unless anyone objects. :thumbsup:
